name: Li Wenbin
current_role: Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer, Lee & Man Paper Manufacturing Ltd (HKEX: 2314)
profile: Li Wenbin (Lee Man Bun, MH JP; also known as Edmond Lee) is the younger son of Lee & Man founder Lee Wan Keung Patrick and brother of chairman Raymond Lee Man Chun. He has run Hong Kong-listed Lee & Man Paper, one of China's largest containerboard/tissue makers, as CEO since about 2013-14, and his family holds a large stake.
interesting_fact: Lee & Man Paper is one of Asia's largest packaging-paper producers, with mills across mainland China plus operations in Vietnam and Malaysia; the Lee family also controls sister firm Lee & Man Chemical.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a chemical engineer at the University of British Columbia, and was already an executive director and assistant general manager of the family paper company at age 26 (2005/06 annual report).
notes: Hurun lists him jointly with Ho Tsz Wan. No personal channels found; route via Lee & Man Paper head office (39/F Lee & Man Commercial Center, North Point, HK) / company secretary. UBC degree per MarketScreener profile.

name: Tung Ching Sai
current_role: Executive Director and CEO, Xinyi Glass Holdings (HKEX: 868); chairman of Xinyi Electric Storage; director at Xinyi Solar/Xinyi Energy
profile: Tung Ching Sai has been CEO of Hong Kong-listed Xinyi Glass, a maker of float, automotive and architectural glass whose customers include Ford, GM and VW, since 2004. He is the brother of vice-chairman Tung Ching Bor and brother-in-law of founder-chairman Lee Yin Yee; he also chairs the group's energy-storage arm.
interesting_fact: Beyond glass, he sits across the Xinyi group's clean-energy businesses (Xinyi Solar, Xinyi Energy) and chairs Xinyi Electric Storage, a natural fit for an energy-focused conversation.
deep_cut_fact: Xinyi Glass's own annual report styles him 'Tan Sri Datuk' Tung Ching Sai, i.e. he holds Malaysian honorific titles, unusual for a Hong Kong/mainland industrialist (Xinyi has major manufacturing in Malaysia).
notes: Low public profile; no personal channels found. Route via Xinyi Glass company secretary / IR in Hong Kong. Energy angle: Xinyi Solar and Xinyi Electric Storage. Malaysian manufacturing link stated as general context, not individually verified.

name: Wang Wenhui
current_role: Director and co-controlling shareholder, Guangzhou Ruoyuchen Technology (SZSE: 003010)
profile: Wang Wenhui (b. 1985) co-founded Guangzhou e-commerce services firm Ruoyuchen in 2011 with her husband, chairman/CEO Wang Yu; together they control roughly 43%. Ruoyuchen began as a cross-border/online store operator for international brands and has pivoted to its own brands such as LYCOCELLE (home care) and FineNutri (supplements). She has been a director since 2017.
interesting_fact: Ruoyuchen's growth has shifted from running Tmall/JD stores for foreign brands to building its own consumer brands (LYCOCELLE laundry care, FineNutri, NuiBay).
deep_cut_fact: Ruoyuchen started in May 2011 with registered capital of just RMB 100,000: she and Wang Yu each put in RMB 50,000. She served as the company's supervisor until 2015 and is also listed as its senior adviser on employee career development.
notes: Hurun lists her jointly with husband Wang Yu, who is the public face (chairman). Best route is via Ruoyuchen's board secretary / IR. Not on-theme for energy/data centers.

name: Chen Chenghui
current_role: Chairman, Kehua Data Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 002335), Xiamen; also chairs Kehua Digital Energy (Kehua Shuneng)
profile: Chen Chenghui (b. 1960, Pinghe, Fujian) is a PhD, professor-level electrical engineer who built Kehua (formerly Kehua Hengsheng) from a Zhangzhou instrument factory into a major maker of UPS power systems, data-center infrastructure, solar inverters and energy storage. He has been chairman since 2010 and holds ~17% of the company.
interesting_fact: Kehua is squarely in the podcast's lane: it supplies UPS/critical power and builds and operates data centers (IDC), and its Kehua Digital Energy arm sells PV inverters and battery storage systems.
deep_cut_fact: Before Kehua, he was deputy director of the Zhangzhou Kelong Electronic Instrument Factory (hence the 'Kelong' in some rich-list entries). He is a National Model Worker, May 1st Labour Medal winner and sat on the first expert committee of the China Power Supply Society.
notes: Highly relevant for energy/data-center podcast. Route via board secretary (Lin Tao) in Xiamen; company also runs overseas marketing that may handle English-language media.

name: Zheng Hanjie
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Guangdong T&K Pharmaceutical (Tai En Kang, SZSE: 301263), Shantou
profile: Zheng Hanjie co-controls (with Sun Weiwen) Shantou-based T&K Pharmaceutical, founded in 1999 as a drug distributor/agency business that later added its own factories and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2022. He is now steering it from generics toward innovative drugs, notably CKBA for vitiligo, developed with Shanghai Jiao Tong University.
interesting_fact: He calls T&K's push into innovative drugs a long-held goal: the firm began in distribution only because it lacked capital for R&D or factories, and he now targets R&D at 10-20% of revenue.
deep_cut_fact: He is a trained physician: he studied three years of traditional Chinese medicine followed by four years of Western medicine and practised as a doctor before going into business.
notes: Hurun lists him jointly with Sun Weiwen (co-controller). Gives media interviews (NBD 2025). Pharma, not energy; route via board secretary Li Ting at the IR email.

name: Jason Chen
current_role: Chairman and President, Test Research, Inc. (TRI, TWSE: 3030), Taipei
profile: Jason Chen (Chen Chieh-yuan) co-founded Taipei-based Test Research Inc. (TRI) in 1989 with colleagues from RCA's test division. TRI grew from in-circuit testers into a one-stop supplier of PCB-assembly inspection gear (ICT, ATE, AOI/AXI, semiconductor test) used by Foxconn, ASUS, Quanta and others; it listed in Taiwan in 2002 and he still serves as chairman and president.
interesting_fact: TRI's AOI optical-inspection line took about five years and three project leaders before it sold anything; Chen cites it as proof that decisive commitment matters in equipment businesses.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in RCA's automatic-test department in Taiwan; when RCA pulled back he co-founded TRI and coded in a small apartment on Zhongshan North Road. Business Today called him the industry's 'software R&D king': his 518F DOS test software became an industry standard.
notes: Taiwanese (list says China). Company spokesperson is Lin Chiang-huai (long-time VP). TRI inspection equipment is used in AI-server/electronics manufacturing, a data-center supply-chain angle.

name: Sir Martin Franklin
current_role: Founder & CEO, Mariposa Capital (Miami family office); founder/chairman Element Solutions; co-founder/co-chairman Nomad Foods
profile: London-born, Miami-based serial dealmaker Martin Franklin (b. 1964) built Jarden from ~$300m to $10bn+ revenue before selling it to Newell in 2016. He co-founded Nomad Foods (Birds Eye, Findus), built Element Solutions (ex-Platform Specialty), and has launched multiple SPACs, including J2/APi Group, through Mariposa Capital.
interesting_fact: In July 2026 Solstice Advanced Materials (the Honeywell spin-off) agreed to buy Element Solutions for about $14.5bn including debt, a deal pitched on electronics and AI-hardware infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: He is an extreme endurance athlete: three Ironman World Championships in Kona (2005 in 10h55m), the Badwater Ultramarathon in 41h29m (2007), and the Leadville 100 run and MTB race. He told the FT: 'I have my best ideas on a bicycle, or running over a mountain.'
notes: 'Sir' is an Antiguan knighthood (KGCN, 2018) for work in Antigua & Barbuda, where he was Special Economic Envoy; not a UK honour. Other deep cuts: youngest VP in Rothschild US history; CEO of NYSE-listed Benson Eyecare at 28. Mariposa Capital site not reachable; route via Element Solutions or Nomad Foods corporate offices.

name: Xu Na
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Hangzhou XZB Tech Co., Ltd. (SSE: 603040)
profile: Xu Na (b. 1969), a male internal-combustion-engine engineer, founded Hangzhou XZB in 2002 as a maker of valve cotters (lock clips) and grew it into a Shanghai-listed supplier of precision valve-train components for engine makers. He co-controls the company with Hu Xin and has run it as chairman and GM since 2010.
interesting_fact: XZB specialises in tiny precision engine parts (valve collets, valve-train components) and is designated a 'core technical staff' role for its chairman as well as the boss.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as a technician in the technical department of the research institute at the Hangzhou Automobile Engine Factory, and studied internal-combustion engines, before founding XZB (originally 'Hangzhou XZB Lock Clip Co.') in 2002.
notes: Low profile. Board secretary is Zheng Xiaoling (VP). Web search budget ran out mid-lane; profile based on exchange-disclosed bio via 10jqka.

name: Xie Shuli
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shanghai YCT Electronics Group (Yachuang Dianzi, SZSE: 301099)
profile: Xie Shuli (b. 1972), a Tongji University chemistry graduate, built Shanghai YCT Electronics from a component trading firm (run as GM from 2001) into a listed authorised distributor of electronic components, largely for automotive customers, which now also designs its own analog and mixed-signal chips (power management, drivers, automotive CIS). He controls about 52% of the company.
interesting_fact: YCT has moved up the value chain from pure distribution into in-house chip design (power-management, signal-chain and mixed-signal SoCs), alongside distributing memory, MCUs and passives.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating in chemistry from Tongji University in 1996, his first job was as a sales manager at Shantou Ultrasonic printed-circuit-board company (1996-99), before he became a director of Hong Kong Taixin and later GM of Shanghai YCT.
notes: Hurun's 'YCL' appears to be YCT (Shanghai Yct Electronics, 雅创电子); name and Chinese characters match the chairman/controller. Board secretary/CFO: Fan Xiaolei. Web search budget ran out; bio from exchange-disclosed data.

name: Liao Xinyu
current_role: Individual shareholder (top-10 holder, ~0.45%) of Foshan Haitian Flavouring & Food (SSE: 603288); no executive role found
profile: Liao Xinyu (廖忻愉) appears in Foshan Haitian Flavouring & Food's disclosures as a top-10 shareholder holding about 26.1 million A-shares (~0.45%) of China's largest soy-sauce maker. No executive or board role at Haitian was found; Hurun listed her wealth from Haitian in 2020-22.
interesting_fact: Haitian, controlled by Pang Kang and fellow managers via Guangdong Haitian Group, is China's largest condiment maker; its controlling group includes a Liao (Liao Changhui), though no relationship to Liao Xinyu is established in the sources checked.
notes: Passive, private shareholder with no public profile; alive status unknown. No outreach channel of her own found. Only route would be indirect via Haitian IR, which is not appropriate for a private shareholder. Web search budget exhausted; not researched further.

name: Chen Mingjin
current_role: Chairman, Golden Dragon Group (Macau); CPPCC National Committee member; chairman of the board of City University of Macau
profile: Chen Mingjin (Chan Meng Kam, b. 1962, Jinjiang, Fujian) moved to Macau at 17, worked in a factory, then founded Golden Dragon Group in 1990, starting from a casino VIP room and expanding into the Golden Dragon hotel, San Miu supermarkets, travel and appliance trading. He was a directly elected Macau legislator (2005-17), founded the United Citizens Association of Macau, and sits on the national CPPCC.
interesting_fact: He turned the Macau Fujian fellow-townsmen association into a major community and political network for Fujianese immigrants, which carried him to three terms as a directly elected legislator.
deep_cut_fact: An avid golfer, he gave away more than HK$1 million after scoring a hole-in-one in 2015. He also chairs the board of City University of Macau and of Liming Vocational University in Quanzhou, and grew up in a farming family in Ludong village, Dongshi.
notes: Prominent Macau establishment figure, publicly accessible via community associations and City University of Macau. Gaming/hospitality/retail rather than energy. Facebook link listed on Wikipedia, verified status not confirmed.

name: Wang Zhenyu
current_role: Unverified; Hurun attributes wealth to CDH (CDH Investments, Beijing private-equity firm); not on CDH's current management team page
profile: Hurun China (2015-21) listed Wang Zhenyu (王振宇) with wealth from CDH Investments, the Beijing private-equity firm spun out of CICC's direct-investment unit in 2002 by Wu Shangzhi and five other founding partners. CDH's current leadership page does not list him, and his role and current position could not be confirmed with the sources available.
interesting_fact: CDH's first independent fund (US$102m, 2003) backed Li Ning, Focus Media and Mengniu Dairy and reportedly returned about 3.5x.
notes: Identity not confirmed: common name, and web search budget ran out before he could be tied to a specific CDH role (possibly an early partner who has since left). Verify before outreach. Contact form is CDH's general one.

name: Huang Youlong
current_role: Private investor (Singapore national); no current listed-company executive role confirmed
profile: Huang Youlong (b. 1976, Shaodong, Hunan) is a Singapore-based investor who started in the cement trade in Guangdong and, from the 2010s, took stakes in Hong Kong-listed companies (e.g. Sunlon/Shunlong Holdings) and resource ventures, including Mongolian cement and energy. Hurun (2015-19) listed him jointly with actress Zhao Wei, his wife at the time.
interesting_fact: He grew up in a farming family in Longtang village, Shetianqiao town, Hunan, and made his first money in the Guangdong cement business.
notes: Not recommended as an outreach target: very private, and his public record is dominated by the 2018 CSRC penalty (5-year securities-market ban over the Wanjia Culture bid) and media scrutiny. He and Zhao Wei divorced in 2021. No published contact channel.

name: Yao Junhong
current_role: Founder and CEO, Souche (Dasouche / Hangzhou Dasouche Auto Service Co.), Hangzhou
profile: Yao Junhong founded Hangzhou-based Souche (大搜车), an auto-services unicorn that Hurun listed among its unicorn founders in 2019-21. Souche now pitches itself as 'AI application infrastructure for China's used-car industry': dealer-management SaaS (claimed ~90% share), OEM user-operation systems, a used-car B2B auction platform, inspection services and vehicle delivery.
interesting_fact: Souche says its dealer operating system is used by about 90% of China's used-car dealers, and its delivery network covers 2,600+ districts and counties (company data to end-2025).

public_contacts.value: https://www.dasouche.com (has 联系我们/合作洽谈 contact pages and an investor-relations section; main line 0571-88607326)

notes: Web search budget and Wikipedia access ran out for this person, so his background was not independently verified beyond the Hurun record and company site. Souche's site now has an investor-relations section; check for a recent listing and IR contact. 'AI infrastructure' framing may suit the podcast.
